title: Titanium Compressor Blisk
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this engine component application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by integral bladed compressor disk (blisk) and service environment demands.
process: 5-axis CNC roughing for engine component geometry
Wire EDM contour profiling with Class 6g gauge
CMM per AS9102 with Class 6g gauge

commonFailures: SCC in chloride-rich marine atmosphere - controlled by bake-out 300C + corrosion-inhibiting primer — critical for integral bladed compressor performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Compressor Blisk suitable for Integral bladed compressor disk (blisk)?
faq.a: Titanium Compressor Blisk uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address engine component operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Compressor Blisk?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Compressor Blisk is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for integral bladed compressor requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Compressor Blisk require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. integral bladed compressor components require Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service — tailored for integral bladed compressor application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Compressor Blisk shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Compressor Blisk includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet integral bladed compressor specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Blisk / Compressor disk engine component components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
